contract: plugins/default/audit-jsonl of the chaperone repository, docs/design.md 5.4
notes: The input is one audit file and one call. args.file is the bytes of the file in one of the forms text, base64 and repeat. args.file of null stands for a path with no file.
args.filter, args.offset and args.limit are the arguments of the entry point. An empty filter value takes each call.
The reader reads the last 4194304 bytes of the file at most. When the file is longer, it drops the text before the first LF of the part that it reads.

The reader ends a line at LF only. It does not read the text after the last LF. It skips a line that holds only the six bytes of ASCII whitespace. It gives each other line to the JSON reader with each of its bytes.

A record is a JSON object with the nine keys of the Rust sink and no other key. run is 32 lower-case hex digits. call is an integer of 1 or more. started and time are RFC 3339 times. app is null or a slug of the chaperone. tool is <unknown> or an exposed name. arguments_sha256 is 64 lower-case hex digits. event is one of decided, ran, waiting, delivered and failed. detail has the form that its event takes.

value.rows is one row for each call, newest first: the reader orders the calls by the newest record of each call. The records of one call have one run and one call number. steps is the records of a call, oldest first.

decision comes from the decided record, and is null when the reader did not read that record. gate is the gate ID of the first record whose detail names a gate. reason is the deny code or the fault code. outcome is the event of the newest record. ended is the time of the newest record.
A line that is no record makes a row with a problem, and each filter takes that row. The records of one call that disagree on started, app, tool or arguments_sha256 make one such row.
value.lines_read is the count of lines that the reader read. value.has_more is true when the filter takes more calls than offset and limit show.

A problem is an object. class is one of none, missing, unreadable, too large, not JSON, not an object, refused, unreachable, not a record and capped. capped is a notice: the reader stopped at a limit and kept what it read before.

text is the sentence that a page shows. A problem of the class not JSON has no text: its sentence ends with a message of the JSON reader of Python. It has start, the part of the sentence before that message.
